question: On the square, triangular, honeycomb and kagome ring boards, is the route reading's polygon the same shape as the board's graph-distance polygon, and if not, which is rounder?

definitions.route polygon: conv{disp(C)/len(C)} over the simple cycles C of the contact quotient of the route digraph (a hop of g cells from one contact to the next counterclockwise on a ring), in lattice coordinates (BOARD-READ-20261110-001A's theorem).
definitions.graph polygon: The same over the simple cycles of the ring-graph quotient (rings adjacent through contacts, an edge not reused).
definitions.homothetic: route polygon = s times graph polygon for some s > 0: the route reading is the board's graph metric up to scale and a constant.
definitions.anisotropy: max over directions of the gauge of a Euclidean unit vector divided by its min (3,600 directions): 1 for a disc, 2/sqrt 3 = 1.1547 for a regular hexagon, sqrt 2 = 1.4142 for a square.
definitions.rounder: route anisotropy below graph anisotropy by more than 1e-6.

public_inputs.run: run.py in this folder, 6 worker processes.
public_inputs.family: Boards square, triangular, honeycomb, kagome; g = 2 to 6; for the second method, breadth-first distances on the 48 x 48-domain torus from one ring of the first vertex type to its translates k v, for every primitive v with |v_x|, |v_y| <= 3 and k |v|_inf <= 20.

forbidden_inputs: Changing boards, g, directions, torus size or criteria after seeing results
primary_observable: Per board and g: the two hulls, homothety, anisotropies, and the deviations T - N and d - N_G.
cheapest_meaningful_control: The square board: CONF-METRIC-20261110-001A's Lemma 1 gives the route polygon (1/2g) times the taxicab diamond, homothetic to the graph polygon, anisotropy sqrt 2 for both.
decision_or_followup_rule: Frozen. Prediction P1: on the square board the polygons are homothetic at every g. Hypothesis H (the coordinator's alternative): on every board read the route polygon is homothetic to the graph polygon, so the route reading is the board's graph metric up to scale and a constant; H fails on a board where they are not homothetic, and that board's reading is then rounder or less round than its graph distance by the anisotropies. The theorem of ticket A is checked here: every deviation T - N and d - N_G must stay bounded (no growth with k); a growing deviation is a gap in the proof.
stop_rule: Stop when every board and g has both methods' readings.
nonclaims: Four periodic boards, g = 2 to 6; the program's ring cells and contact law; declared rings (A45) on a declared board (A51).
feasibility_disclosure: Blind on the results: before freezing only the boards' structures were printed (edges per domain, ring degrees). The square board's polygon is known from CONF-METRIC-20261110-001A.
